advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword the doctor sentence in docs/mcp-client-setup.md: doctor flags literal PATs in the top-level `mcpServers` of `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` and `~/.claude.json` when there is no project `.mcp.json`, but it misses Claude local-scope entries (`projects[...]`) and anything shadowed by a project `.mcp.json`.
evidence: docs/mcp-client-setup.md (added): "`rebar store doctor` does not find these entries: it reads only the top-level `mcpServers` map of the home configs, and skips them when the working directory has a project `.mcp.json`."
src/rebar/_commands/doctor_mcp_client.py:274-276: match = _ENV_REF.match(auth.strip()) / if match is None: / return None, KIND_PAT_LITERAL
advisory.finding: The new 'Keep the PAT off the command line' section says `rebar store doctor` does not find entries saved the old way. That is only true for Claude Code local-scope entries, or when the working directory has a project `.mcp.json`. With no project `.mcp.json`, doctor reads the top-level `mcpServers.rebar` entry of `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` and of `~/.claude.json`. A `copilot mcp add` entry or a `claude mcp add -s user` entry holding an expanded PAT fails `_ENV_REF` there and is reported as `pat-literal-in-config` at severity error.
scenarios: A user who ran the old `copilot mcp add --header "...$MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT"` runs `rebar store doctor` outside a checkout. Doctor reports `pat-literal-in-config` for copilot, which contradicts the guide, so the guide and the tool disagree.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace it with: "`rebar store doctor` cannot be relied on to find these entries: it misses Claude Code local-scope entries (stored per directory inside `~/.claude.json`), and it skips the home configs entirely when the working directory has a project `.mcp.json`. Outside such a checkout it reports a user-level literal PAT as `pat-literal-in-config`."

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a check that every `headers.Authorization` in examples/mcp-clients/*.json uses the `${VAR}` placeholder form, not a bare `$VAR`
evidence: tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:107: `doc = json.loads((REPO_ROOT / ".mcp.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))` (load_copilot reads the root config, not the example)
tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:102: `re.sub(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}|\$([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", repl, value)` (accepts the bare `$VAR` form too)
tests/unit/test_review_bot_git_credential_argv.py:314-317: the new example scan reads only `$comment`, not `mcpServers.*.headers`
advisory.finding: No test pins the Copilot example config's change from `$MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI` to `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}` (the form the commit says the client expands). The facade config tests load only the repo-root .mcp.json. Their `_expand_env` helper also accepts both `$VAR` and `${VAR}`. So if the example went back to `"Bearer $MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI"`, every test would still pass.
scenarios: Someone edits examples/mcp-clients/copilot/mcp-config.json back to `"Bearer $MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI"`. A user copies it into ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json, as the guide now says to. If Copilot sends the placeholder text instead of expanding it, the user gets a 401, and CI does not notice.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_review_bot_git_credential_argv.py (or the facade config test), walk `mcpServers.*.headers.Authorization` in each examples/mcp-clients/**/*.json and assert it matches `^Bearer \$\{[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\}$`.
